catboost-1wu real-engineering fix, closing catboost-8z4.122's follow-up: added an ERawTargetType::String Pool target path so class_names (STRING class names, e.g. 'neg'/'pos') can be matched against a Pool built from a factor/character label. Rather than switching catboost.load_pool()'s default label encoding for every factor/character label (bigger blast radius, would require every other Pool consumer of an Integer target -- CatBoostPoolGetLabel_R, CatBoostPoolTrainEvalSplit_R's stratified split, CatBoostPoolSlice_R -- to also gain a String branch, and risks the numeric-target training path no longer being bit-identical), scoped this narrowly per catboost-1wu's own design guidance: catboost.from_matrix now stashes the factor/character label's levels() (already computed for SetClassLabels) as an inert 'class_labels' Pool attribute; catboost.train(), only when params$class_names is present (NOT classes_count alone -- that combination already trains against the Pool's existing numeric target via TNumericClassTargetConverter and must keep doing so unpromoted) AND that attribute exists, calls the new native CatBoostPoolPromoteStringTarget_R to retarget the Pool's already-built Integer target to String in place, mapping each integer index i back to ClassLabels[i] -- the exact inverse of `as.integer(factor(label)) - 1L` (R/catboost.R), so it round-trips losslessly through native's TUseClassLabelsTargetConverter (target_converter.cpp:210-211) back to the same class index i. catboost.train() undoes this promotion via on.exit(CatBoostPoolDemoteStringTarget_R(...)) right after the native fit call, on both the success and error path, so the mutation never outlives the single catboost.train() call -- fix round 2 closed a real bug where an un-reverted promotion left a Pool permanently String-typed, silently breaking catboost.pool.get_label()/train_eval_split() afterwards, and silently flipping which class index means what on a later class_names-less retrain whenever the factor's levels() weren't alphabetical (both Promote and Demote are also each individually idempotent, so retraining the same Pool object, or passing it as both learn_pool and test_pool, is safe). Every other caller (no class_names, or a non-factor label) is completely untouched -- same code path as before. Scope: catboost.train() only -- catboost.cv/catboost.grid_search/catboost.select_features/etc. do not yet apply this promotion and still hit the original native error for this combination; that gap is out of this ticket's scope (documented in catboost.train's roxygen @note) and tracked as a known follow-up, not silently claimed as closed. Verified directly: catboost.train(catboost.load_pool(X, label=c('neg','pos',...)), params=list(loss_function='MultiClass', classes_count=2, class_names=list('neg','pos'))) now trains without error (including retraining the same Pool object twice, and using it as both learn_pool and test_pool), model$classes_ resolves to c('neg','pos'), and classes_count alone (no class_names) against the same factor-label Pool still trains exactly as before. Fix round 2 additionally verified: after a class_names training call, catboost.pool.get_label() and catboost.pool.train_eval_split(is_classification=TRUE) on the same Pool still work exactly as before (not the promoted-and-never-restored state that fix round 1 left behind); a factor with non-alphabetical levels (e.g. levels=c('pos','neg')) trained once with class_names then retrained WITHOUT class_names on the SAME Pool object produces predictions matching a fresh, never-promoted Pool trained the same way (not the silently class-flipped predictions fix round 1 would have produced). See test_params_validation.R.

tolerance_justification: catboost.select_features() is the same native SelectFeatures entry point the CLI's select-features mode calls (P10.A wiring). catboost-hpk.5 root-caused the loss_graph.loss_values discrepancy documented in the shap_calc_type test's comment (differs from the CLI oracle by ~1.6% relative, at the first entry, before any elimination): CLI's mode_select_features.cpp:107-110 (LoadPools) calls ReorderByTimestampLearnDataIfNeeded then ShuffleLearnDataIfNeeded on the learn pool BEFORE handing it to the shared NCB::SelectFeatures(TCatBoostOptions, ...) entry point (select_features.cpp:219); that entry point's own pool prep (QuantizePools, select_features.cpp:101-168) never shuffles or reorders. R's CatBoostSelectFeatures_R (src/catboostr.cpp:2617-2629) calls the JSON-params overload (select_features.cpp:338-379, same overload Python's Cython wrapper calls per that file's header comment) directly on the pools handed in -- no shuffle step, identical call sequence to Python. Confirmed empirically with tools/oracle/cli/bin/catboost-v1.2.10 on the smoke fixture (tests/fixtures/oracle-cli/smoke_data.csv/.cd, which has one Categ feature so preprocess.cpp's NeedShuffle (preprocess.cpp:161-181) fires unconditionally): passing --has-time (which short-circuits NeedShuffle to false) moves the CLI's own first loss_graph.loss_values entry from 0.4171481374 to 0.4018134644 -- a 3.7% relative move, proving the shuffle alone materially moves the baseline loss on this exact fixture, same order of magnitude as (larger than) the reported discrepancy. R's own value for the identical params (verified via tests/testthat/test_select_features.R's base_call(Exact) helper) is 0.4239361071, which is (0.4239361071-0.4171481374)/0.4171481374 = 1.63% relative to the CLI oracle's 0.4171481374 -- the exact ~1.6% relative figure this ticket set out to explain. Ruled out: shap_calc_type parity (already exact, per the Python-oracle RecursiveByShapValues/RecursiveByLossFunctionChange tests matching at 1e-12, proving R's call path is bit-identical to Python's) and fstr-subset sizing (GetMaxObjectCountForFstrCalc, loss_change_fstr.cpp:84-86, is a no-op on datasets this small). Not fixed: reproducing the CLI's extra shuffle in R would mean deliberately diverging from the shared native entry point Python also uses (matching Python there, not the CLI's incidental preprocessing step, is the actual library-parity contract), and would require bit-exact replication of TRestorableFastRng64(catBoostOptions.RandomSeed) + NCB::Shuffle's permutation from R -- disproportionate for a row whose actual verified contract (selected_features/eliminated_features/removed_features_count) already matches the CLI oracle exactly.
